The Council of the College of Preceptors has
summoned a conference of teachers and friends
of education, to be held at the rooms of the
Society of Arts on the 9th.

Sir Charles Dilke lately moved for a return
"of all lodges, houses, official residences, and
rights of pasture occupied or enjoyed within
any of her Majesty's parks under the charge
of the Commisbioners of her Majesty's Works
and Public Buildinp ; showing the names of
the persons occupying or enjoying the same,
and also the grounds of such occupation or
enjoyment." This has now been published,
and it appears that among the persons occupy-
ing houses "by grace and favour of the
Queen," are the following :—in Bushey-park
—the Duke of NemoUrs, Bushey-house and
gardens; Lord Alfred Paget, Upper-lodge
and gardens; Miss Blake and Miss Campbell,
Hawthorn-lodge. In Greenwich-park—Prince
Arthur, Ranger's•house and grounds. In
Richmond-park—the Duke of Teck, White-
lodge; Earl Russell, Pembroke-lodge; Pro-
fessor Owen, Eabt Sheen-lodge; Lady Bowater,
Thatched-house.

The Minotaur, Hercules, and Not thumber-
land east anchor in Belfast Lough on the 28th
ult.

A mu named Thornway has been murdered
near Macroom, county Cork, and the police
are after the supposed murderer.

Canon Blakcsley is the new dean of Lincoln,
and the Rev. George Rawlinson succeeds to the
canonry of Canterbury thus voided.

The sixty-fifth annual meeting of the Lon-
don Female Penitentiary was held on the 28th
inst. at 166, Pentonville-road, under the presi-
dency of the Earl of Chichester.

On the 2?th ult. the representatives of sixty-
three of the civic guilds, in the persons of their
masters, wardens, and clerks were entertained
by the Lord Mayor and Lady Mayoress at a
banquet in the Egyptian-hall of the Mansion-
house which was served with the customary
civic splendour.

On the 30th ult, a mass of trades unionists,
members of friendly 'societies, and publicans,
was held in Pomona Gardens, Manchester, to
petition for uniformity of hours of closing
public-houses. The advocates of temperance
mustered strongly, and much opposition was
shown. The proceedings wore most up-
roarious. General fighting ensued, and several
persons were thrown off the platform.
Eventually a strong body of police were
gathered, and cleared the hall.

The 28th being the 34th anniversary of her
Majesty's coronation was observed with the
customary honours at Windsor, in the
metropolis, and in the various garrison, towns
and naval arsenals. At Windsor the bells of
St. George's Chapel and St. John's Church
rang merry peals throughout the day, and
Royal salutes were fired in the Long Walk
and in St. James's Park. The usual rejoicings
were loyally observed at Chatham, Sheerness,
Portsmouth, Plymouth, &o.

The success of the nine hours agitation in
the iron and engineering trades was celebrated
on Monday by a dinner at the Crystal
Palace.

Two men wore drowned on the 29th ult. by
the upsetting of a fishing-boat off the Wexford
coast.

It is stated in the weekly report of the
Registrar-General that the mean temperature,
which on Monday, the 24th ult., was 66.3 deg.
and 4.1 dog. above the average was below
the average on each succeeding lay; and was
only ö69 deg. on Wednesday, or in defect by
4.8 deg. Rather less than half an inch of
rain fell at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich,
raising the measured fall in the first half of
this year to 12.3 inches, showing an excess of
rather more than an inch and a half upon the
average fall in 56 years for this portion of the
year.

Last week the mortality from all causes in
London and twenty other large towns of the
United Kingdom was at the rate of 20 deaths
annually to every 1.000 persons estimated to
be living. In the metropolis 2,147 births and
1,070 deaths were. registered; the former
having been 94 and the latter 345 below the
average. So low a death rate has not pre-
vailed in London since the beginning of 1865.
Forty-three persons died. from small-pox, 33
from measles, 11 from scarlet fever, 44 from
whooping-oough, 20 from different forms of
fever (of which 2 were certified as typhus, 14
as enterio or typhoid, and 4 as simple con-
tinued fever), 37 from diarrhcea, and not one
from diphtheria. Diseases of the respiratory
organs caused 292 deaths.

Both Houses of Convocation assembled at
Westminster on Tuesday morning for the
transaction of business. A large number of
petitions for and against the use of the
Athanaiian Creed were presentedi

It is stated that the judgeship of the Corn.
wall county courts vacant by the death of Mr.
Charles Dimes Bevan, has been conferred upon
Mr. Montague Bore, QC., Recorder of Bristol.

On the 27th ult. a report spread in the city
of Chester that a gentleman staying at the
Grosvenor Hotel had committed suicide by
cutting his throat. A. Mr. Charles Gunner,
who has been, it is said, in a desponding state
of mind, had come over from Manchester for
the benefit of his health, and was accompanied
by a friend and man servant. The latter went
to call his master, and, on getting no reply,
entered the room and found him quite dead,
with a frightful gash across his throat.

articles.title: International Bridge (over the Niagara will be finished by September next.
articles.text:
The International Bridge (over the Niagara
will be finished by September next.

A horrible murder was committed at the
Marine Barracks, Chatham, at one o'clock on
Sunday afternoon, by a private named James
Tooth, who deliberately out the throat of a
drummer boy, named George Stock, in the
privateb' library. It appears
_that the man
Tooth heard the deceased say he was going
into the library, and went and concealed
himself. Tooth soon after sprang on him, and
out his throat in such a fearful manner that
the poor fellow died in an hour afterwards.
The man Tooth, when placed in the cells, said
he did it because Stock endeavoured to get
him into trouble. Great sensation has been.
caused in the neighbourhood by this cold-
blooded murder. Tooth has been handed
over to the civil authorities.

All vessels arriving at Gibraltar from
Odessa, and other ports from the Black Sea,
with foul bills of health, are subject to a
quarantine of twenty-one days, and if siok-
ness on board, will bo ordered to quit the
port forthwith.

On Tuesday evening there was a grand
i
choral festival in Westminster Abbey n aid
of the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel
in Foreign Parts.

The nomination for tho Southern division of
the West Riding will take place on Monday
next.

In the Court of Common Pleas, on Tuesday,
a young woman, 22 years of age, the daughter
of a tradesman in the neighbourhood of
Thames-street, brought an action for breach
or promise of marriage against a lioensed
victualler. The jury gave a verdict for £1.50.
A similar ease was heard in the Court of
Exohequer. The plaintiff; 28 years of age,
was the daughter of a carpenter, and the
defendant was formerly one of her father's
lodgers. The compensation was assessed by
the jury at £lOO.

Some time ago a Committee of the Society
of Arts was appointed to consider how far the
existing means of crossing the Channel could
be improved. They have just presented their
report, in which they express an opinion that
although no large measure of improvement can
be effected in the Channel passage unless with
vessels of much greater size, much might be
done in the present mode of conducting the
traffic, Several suggestions are made for the
alleviation of
,the miseries under, which pas-
sengers at present suffer, and amongst these
are a higher order of accommodation and
ventilation, more•commodioue cabin fittings,
and the better regulation of the fish, fruit, an
vegetable traffic. New boats, about 50 feet
longer than the existing vessels, are also
desirable.

From the weekly return of Treasury receipts
and payments, it appears that the expenditure
of the past quarter, which was not included in
the revenue returns issued on Saturday even-
ing, has amounted to £18,175,391 or
£218,116 less than the teoeipts. The balance
in the Bank of England is nearly seven,
millions sterling.

The Bill for the introduction of responsible
government into the Caps colony had passed
the Assembly. The majority for the third
reading was ten, which, comparing the num-
ber of members in the Assembly with those in
the House of Commons, was equal, the Argus
says, to a majority of one hundred in the latter
House.

A dinner was given in Paris the other night
by the Republican Club of the Seine to the
three new Radical members of the French
Assembly who were returned at the recent
eleotious. The principal speech was delivered
by M. Louis Blanc, who maintained that the
only true Conservatives just now were the
Republicans. The reason was that the Re-
publio had nothing to overthrow; whereas no
monarchy could be established without a
revolution. The Republic was the only Govern.
ment compatible with the free exercise of the
sovereign rights of the people. Those rights
being now recogiiised, Republicans had no need
th be aggreasive. In conclusion, M. Louis
Blan‘o bore tebtimony to the fiervices antlered
to the country by M. Thiers.

articles.text:
LATEST INTELLIGENCE.

FRIDAY.
A socialist agitator, named Bohne, has
been arested in the mining district of Dort-
mund, Germany, for delivering incendiary
speeches to the former strike hands.
The Saxon Government has requested, by
Prince Bismarck, to join the Conferences on the
Socialist question to meet at Berlin in the
autumn. Other German Governments will
receive similar invitations.
The Boston Jubilee was largely attended
yesterday. Mr. Greeley was present, and was
heartily cheered. The French hand will give
six concerts in New York, three in Phila-
delphia, and will possibly visit Chicago.
Her Majesty has intimated her intention
of conferring the honour of knighthood on Mr.
G. Gilbert Scott, the eminent architect, on
the occasion of the completion of the Prince
Consort's National Memorial in Hyde-park.
The Press° says that Odillon Barrot
is definitely designated by the Government
for the post of Presidett of the Council of
State.

His Royal Highness the Duke of Edinburgh'
has signified his intention to distribute the
prizes gained in the National Music Compe-
titions at the Crystal Palace to-morrow (Satur-
day) at a quarter past six.
The Perthshire Constitutional says that
Mr. Arthur Kinnaird's seat for the city of
Perth will be contested at the next election.
Mr. Charles E. Lewis, of London, who, it
is said, intends contesting the Parliamentary
representation of Derry In the Conservative
interest, has arrived there, and addressed a
meeting of the Conservative party last
evening.

The Southampton authorities will have to
pay £291 for the services and maintenance of
the metropolitan police sent there to maintain
order during the late sailors' strike; but of
this amount the steam-packet companies will
refund £250.

The Rochester Castle Gardens were opened
to the public on Thursday afternoon by the
Mayor, in the presence of a large company.
A public subscription has been raised for
laying out the gardens and work, which has
already cost more than £2,000.

The camp at Wimbledon is now nearly 06trl
pleted. All the association tents are pitched,
and besides the camps of the Scottish, Eon.
Artillery company, and Victorians, which are
occupied, preparations are now being made
for pitching those of the London Rifle Brigade,
2nd and 3rd London Rifles, Queen's, St.
George's, and several other corps which have
obtained permission to have their regimental
camps in the enelosure. Most of the Volunteers
will go under canvas on Sunday next.

A meeting, attended by about 3,ooopersons,
was held at Leeds on Monday night, to discuss
the merits of the Government Licensing Bill.
reiolution was submitted declaring that the
number of public-houses should be reduced
and the hours shortened. A counter-proposi-
tion was made by the publicans, which after a
close vote, was declared to be lost, and the
original resolution earned. The meeting then
broke up in great confusion.
It is said that the Bishopric of Sierra Leone
is about to become vaoant by the resignation
of the Right Rev. Dr. Cheatham.
Herr Brunner, President of the Swiss
National Council (who was on Monday to have
opened the Council in person), on entering his
house in the dark fell through a low open
window on the staircase into the courtyard
below, and was injured very seriously ii the
back of the bead.

Seventy-five deaths from sunstroke °conned
in New York on Tuesday last, and forty-five
yesterday.
The Belfast Newsletter is informed that the
Irish Executive, for the first time since corn
-
missions have issued, has omitted the name of
the Mayor of Drogheda from th,^ rresept for
holding the ensuing assizes in that bounty
town.

Sir E. Bardley Wilraot, Recorder of War.
wiok, has been selected as the Conservative
candidate for South Warwickshire, in the
room of Mr. H. C. Wise, who is about to
retire. Mr. John Hardy will also not stand
again for this division of Warwickshire. The
Liberal candidates selected are Sir R. N. C.
Hamilton, Bart., LB., who was Tian°.
cessfal at the last election by a small majority,
and Mr. Thomas Lloyd, High Sheriff and
county banker, an advanced Liberal.
William Holmes, a bank manager, has
been sentenced by the Cumberland Quarter
Sessions to five years' penal servitude for
embezzling £3,000 from his employers, Messrs.
Carrick, Lee, and Sons, bankers and solicitors,
of Brampton._
- -

Mr. Silolto V. Hare, who has several times
contested the representation of Bristol, has,
owing to ill•health, decided not to offer him-
self as a candidate at the next election. A
committee of Conservatives has been appointed
to wait on Mr. Hare to endeavour to induce
hint to reconsider his determination,
